title: Snow would not settle on the saucer (airman Donald Bass)

tellings.quote: Snow blows sideways through the site. It gathers on the ground, on the rocks, but not on the craft. Snow strikes the saucer and disappears. Nothing accumulates. That detail comes from a young airman on perimeter security named Donald Bass.

plain: At a crashed saucer said to have come down in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948, snow reportedly blew across the site and piled up on the ground and rocks but vanished as soon as it touched the craft, so none built up on it. Michels tells this as he narrates the crash story, and he credits the detail to a young airman on perimeter security named Donald Bass. It suggests the object was giving off heat or some other energy.
